TWO compounds, DIFFERENT descriptions — (R)- is 'lily of the valley, floral, sweet, watery, powdery, ozone-like', (S)- is 'lily of the valley, fruity, green, watery, aldehydic-like'. REVIEW-RULES: split with P, then do each alone. 'less preferred' is judgement, not a descriptor.
Ingredient enumeration — 'one may cite perfuming co-ingredients... decanal, dodecanal, 2-methyl-undecanal'. Lists what may be blended in; attributes no odour to any of them.

Attribution is to the compound: 'it has a prominent menthol odor'. BORDERLINE — the frame is a prior-art citation (1937, pages 589-594), which EXCLUDE normally rejects. Kept because the subject of the odour claim is the named compound, not the citation. Your call.
'is used to impart a eucalyptus leaf note' — REVIEW-RULES keeps the impart form: the note originates in X, it is not a blend effect.
'is used to impart a grapefruit and black currant note'. 'black currant' is not in the ontology — it will land in unmapped descriptors as a candidate.
Same claim as row 300, restated for the composition list. Duplicate content, still a valid row.
Same claim as row 303, restated. Duplicate content, still a valid row.
Two compounds SHARING one description — REVIEW-RULES: add both, approve once. 'slightly' is intensity and is not captured.
'is suitable as an odoriferous and aroma substance having a hay-like note' — odour attributed to the named compound.
Composition-level. Describes what the compound is incorporated INTO ('peppermint or spearmint aroma compositions'), not what it smells of.
Comparative AND blend effect — 'more intense coumarinic and a less pronounced hay-like note IN THE COMBINATION WITH'. Magnitude and change, in a mixture.
Anaphora — the subject is 'This feedstock', which names nothing. 4-phenylpentan-2-ol appears only as a blending partner. Same shape as t11 in the test set.

Odour attributed to the named compound. 'pheromone' is a substance class, not a smell quality. 'completely devoid of any fecal note' is NEGATION — fecal must NOT be captured; capturing it would assert the opposite of the sentence.
Lists compounds by FUNCTION — 'acting as an odour masking agent and as an antibacterial'. No odour is attributed to any of them.
DESCR_COLON form. '(XII)' is a pointer and is left out of the span; the systematic name is complete on its own.

DESCR_COLON form. Dropped strong/radiant/attractive/natural — intensity and judgement. NOTE: the sentence runs on into 'EXAMPLE 2 Perfume Oil Composition...', a sentence-splitting artefact; the odour clause is intact. sandalwood needs 2 molecules.
'can leave a delicate soft odor on the skin' — attributed to the named compound. 'delicate' is judgement and is not captured. '(1a)' is a pointer, left out.
'derivatives' is a FAMILY, not a molecule — REVIEW-RULES rejects 'derivatives of X'. Compounded by 'with an absence of bitterness and odour', which is negation.
Precursor releasing something else — 'towels washed with [the base] exhibit a strong 2-methylundecanal note'. REVIEW-RULES names this exact shape as a reject.
Blend effect — 'the COMBINATION of 8-drimanol with a specific polycyclic woody-amber fragrance can ENHANCE the odor'. The softness and warmth are attributed to natural ambergris, not to the compound.
Anaphora — 'This compound' names nothing. 8-drimanol appears only as the structural comparison.
'peculiar bad smell, bitter taste' is judgement, not a smell quality. The sentence is about a formulation limitation, not an odour description.
Odour attributed to the named compound. Dropped 'strong' (intensity) and 'natural' (judgement). '(Structure III)' is a pointer, left out.
Odour attributed to the named compound. Dropped 'strong'. '(Structure V)' is a pointer, left out.
